precepts.text: Joshua was valiant in the wars and set Israel in their inheritance.
precepts.point: Joseph saved Israel in the famine and Joshua of Ephraim divided the land. Ephraim therefore felt more entitled than Judah, and the rivalry began long before the split.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
“Jesus the son a Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God”. This is Joshua. He fought for us to gain the land and possession promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them”, the ones who did not belong in the land, “that he might set Israel in their inheritance.” Joshua was used to set us in our promised land through war, as David did later as king.

Joshua 8 shows him valiant in the wars. At Ai, when the men of the city looked back and saw the smoke of their city rising to heaven, “they had no power to flee this way or that way”, and Israel smote them until none remained: twelve thousand fell that day. “And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide”, and they raised a great heap of stones over him at the gate.

“Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron”. All Israel, “as well the stranger, as he that was born among them”, stood “half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”, and there they received the blessings and the cursings of the law.

Ebal and Gerizim, like Ai, Bethel and Shechem, are in Ephraim’s land. And Joshua himself was of Ephraim. The one who set Israel in their inheritance and divided the land came from that tribe, which is part of why Ephraim felt so entitled.

precepts.text: The fame of Joshua: the sun stood by his means, and the great Lord heard him.
precepts.point: Take pride in this: we are the descendants of the most famous men on the face of the earth. Our forefathers are mentioned in every single nation, and everybody wants to lay claim to them and to our book. That is why all nations hate us, and we will be famous again: the Most High will get Israel praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame, when he turns back our captivity before our eyes. Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place.

note.label: Joshua 12: The Thirty and One Kings

precepts.why:
In Ecclesiasticus Joshua is called “Jesus the son a Nave”, for Joshua translated into the Greek is Jesus, and Nave is Nun: Joshua the son of Nun. He “was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God, and taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, that he might set Israel in their inheritance.”

“How great glory gat he, when he did lift up his hands, and stretched out his sword against the cities! Who before him so stood to it? for the Lord himself brought his enemies unto him. Did not the sun go back by his means? and was not one day as long as two?” He said, Sun, be thou still, and there were two days of sunlight on the earth. “He called upon the most high Lord, when the enemies pressed upon him on every side; and the great Lord heard him.”

“And with hailstones of mighty power he made the battle to fall violently upon the nations, and in the descent of Beth-horon he destroyed them that resisted, that the nations might know all their strength, because he fought in the sight of the Lord, and he followed the Mighty One.” That is the fame of the man who smote thirty and one kings.

precepts.text: Joshua and Caleb, the two preserved of six hundred thousand, that all Israel might see it is good to follow the Lord.
precepts.point: Take pride in this: we are the descendants of the most famous men on the face of the earth. Our forefathers are mentioned in every single nation, and everybody wants to lay claim to them and to our book. That is why all nations hate us, and we will be famous again: the Most High will get Israel praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame, when he turns back our captivity before our eyes. note.label: Joshua 12: The Thirty and One Kings

precepts.why:
His counterpart Caleb was a mighty man too. “In the time of Moses also he did a work of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Jephunne, in that they withstood the congregation, and withheld the people from sin, and appeased the wicked murmuring. And of six hundred thousand people on foot, they two were preserved to bring them in to the heritage, even unto the land that floweth with milk and honey.”

“The Lord gave strength also unto Caleb, which remained with him unto his old age: so that he entered upon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an heritage: That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” The Most High gave Caleb strength unto his old age, fighting in his eighties like he was in his twenties, and you will read of his strength in the next few chapters. Joshua and Caleb, the two preserved of six hundred thousand, that all Israel might see it is good to follow the Lord.

precepts.text: Samuel established the kingdom, judged the congregation by the law, and by his loyalty was found a true prophet.
precepts.point: Samuel was one of the most respected prophets in the whole history of the prophets: he established the kingdom and anointed Saul, and by his faithfulness he was found a true prophet. Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, but Samuel stayed loyal to the Most High, just as Abraham's faith was tried again and again and he remained faithful.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
“Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, beloved of his Lord, established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.” Samuel was one of the most respected prophets in the whole history of the prophets: he established the kingdom and anointed Saul.

“By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord had respect unto Jacob. By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet.” Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, but Samuel stayed loyal to the Most High.

That tried loyalty is why, when “Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel”, “the Lord heard him.”

precepts.text: The Apocrypha records this very history: the sucking lamb offered, the enemies pressing on every side, and the Lord thundering from heaven.
precepts.point: Samuel was one of the most respected prophets in the whole history of the prophets: he established the kingdom and anointed Saul, and by his faithfulness he was found a true prophet. Faithfulness translates loyalty. He came up under Eli, watched Eli's sons go wicked, Eli die, and the nation take losses, but Samuel stayed loyal to the Most High, just as Abraham's faith was tried again and again and he remained faithful.

note.label: 1 Samuel 7: Put Away the Strange Gods, and the Lord Thundered

precepts.why:
The Apocrypha records this very history: “He called upon the mighty Lord, when his enemies pressed upon him on every side, when he offered the sucking lamb. And the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard.”

That is Mizpeh. “Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the Lord”, and as he was offering it the Philistines drew near to battle, “but the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them.”

That was no regular thunder; it was the Lord entering the battle himself, his voice made to be heard. Israel had repented and put away the false gods, and the prayer of the righteous man reached his ears, so now the Philistines had to deal with the Most High.

moments.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

points: Jesus the son of Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God, and taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, that he might set Israel in their inheritance. Jesus the son of Nave, which is Joshua. For the saving of the elect of God, God sent Joshua.
How great glory gat he, when he did lift up his hands, and stretched out his sword against the cities!
Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, beloved of his Lord, established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.
By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord had respect unto Jacob. God had respect unto Jacob. That precepts down to Acts 10 and Exodus 2.
By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision. God sent Samuel.
Jesus the son of Nave, Joshua, successor of Moses in prophecy, was made great for the saving of the elect of God and for setting Israel in their inheritance.
